races.display_title: Navan Racecourse Nursery Handicap
races.verdict: HOWLIN WOLF continued a theme of race-by-race progression when opening his account on nursery debut at the Curragh recently and with better still to come, Jack Davison's charge earns the tentative nod to follow up. There are plenty of nursery debutants in opposition however, Supreme Lord and Prince of Peppard the pair put forward to chase him home before the benefit of market clues. HOWLIN WOLF (IRE) SUPREME LORD (IRE) PRINCE OF PEPPARD (IRE)

races.display_title: Navan Racing Festival Early Bird Tickets On Sale Now Handicap
races.verdict: A fiendishly-competitive sprint in which one final chance is given to ALL THE GIRLS to prove she's as good on turf as on synthetics having run a cracker from 7 lb out of the weights when finishing runner-up at Dundalk recently. Cool Azul continues to go from strength to strength so he may well emerge as the biggest threat, with Jon Riggens and Gotta Catch'em All another couple worth considering. ALL THE GIRLS (IRE) COOL AZUL (IRE) JON RIGGENS (IRE)

races.display_title: Follow AtTheRaces On X Nursery
races.verdict: NO MORE PINO was unlucky not to finish closer when fourth of 13 on his nursery debut at Kempton last week and, with that appealing as solid form for the grade, he's put forward as the selection. Magical Life had a few of these behind when bolting up at Kempton on her penultimate outing and is respected back down in class. Whiskey Galore has a decent pedigree and could raise his game now switching to nursery company. NO MORE PINO (IRE) MAGICAL LIFE WHISKEY GALORE

races.display_title: Racing Again Wednesday 9th Sept Handicap (Div 1)
races.verdict: This is wide open and it could be worth siding with TAYLORMADE LAD who took this prize a year ago off a 2 lb higher mark and should prove suited by stepping back up in trip after his latest Ayr seventh. Vampire Slayer is next on the list back in this sphere after a layoff with the potential for improvement having improved over hurdles in the winter. Riddikulus and Dr Rio also need factoring in. TAYLORMADE LAD (IRE) VAMPIRE SLAYER (IRE) RIDDIKULUS

races.verdict: ADELAIDE BAY has been pretty expensive to follow since rejoining Chapple-Hyam but this doesn't look much of a race and he can build on last month's encouraging fourth at Newcastle to notch an overdue first success of the year. races.verdict: No shortage of chances in a competitive affair but CARRON found only a subsequent winner too strong on his final start for George Boughey at Yarmouth in June and, boasting a particularly appealing record on all-weather (3 wins from 4 starts) he could be the answer on debut for Ruth Carr. That said, Mr Noble and Haaderr are 2 improving 3-y-os who command plenty of respect, with Pietro another needing consideration back from a break. CARRON (IRE) MR NOBLE (IRE) HAADERR
